settings_languages_intro: The interface speaks every enabled language: a signed-in user gets the language they chose, everyone else the best match for their browser, otherwise the default language. New pages and documents start with the default language as their content language, and every schema label needs a text in it.
settings_languages_enabled_desc: The default language always stays enabled. Translations in a disabled language are kept.
settings_languages_default_desc: For visitors whose browser asks for no enabled language, for new content, and as the language every label must have. Existing content keeps its language.
settings_languages_save_failed: The languages could not be saved.

settings_integration_connections_desc: Accounts people connected themselves, to see their own content on pages. A new address ends those made for the old one.
settings_integration_disconnect_all_body: Every person's connection is removed here at once, and the service is asked to forget each access. People can connect again.

Every person's connection is removed here at once. The integration is off, so the service can't be asked to forget the accesses: each stays valid there until removed in that account's security settings. Turn the integration on first to have them forgotten.
settings_integration_disconnected_unaske: Connections removed: {count}. The service could not be asked to forget {unasked} of them — each stays valid there until removed in that account's security settings.
settings_integration_connections_dropped: Connections made for the previous address were removed: {count}
settings_integration_save_failed: The settings could not be saved.

settings_integration_problem_origin_inva: Enter the address alone, like https://cloud.example.org — without a path or a login.
settings_integration_problem_origin_inse: The address must start with https://.
settings_integration_problem_no_secret_k: This server has no key to protect the integration's credentials (APP_SECRET_KEY). Whoever runs it has to set one first.
integration_grant_expired: This link has expired. Open the file again from its page.
integration_grant_renew: This link was made for an account connection that has changed since. Open the file again from its page.
settings_connections_intro: Your own accounts at the services this site shows content from. Once you connect one, pages show you what the service lets you see there — and show it to you alone.
settings_connections_empty: No service on this site offers connections.
settings_connections_unavailable: {service} is not set up on this site.
settings_connections_waiting: Waiting for you to approve in {service} …
settings_connections_revoked: {service} no longer accepts this connection. Connect again to see your own content there.
settings_connections_moved: This connection was made for another {service} address than the one set up now. Connect again.
settings_connections_remote_kept: Disconnected here, but {service} could not be asked to forget the access. Remove “{client}” in your {service} account’s security settings.
settings_connections_failed_expired: The approval took too long. Start again.
settings_connections_failed_disabled: {service} was turned off on this site in the meantime.
settings_connections_failed_foreign_serv: {service} named another server than the one set up here, so nothing was connected.

settings_connections_failed_unreachable: {service} could not be reached. Try again later.
settings_connections_failed_refused: {service} did not start a connect. Try again later.
settings_connections_failed_no_key: This server has no key to protect the access (APP_SECRET_KEY). Whoever runs it has to set one first.

settings_profile_name_desc: Shown in the app bar and wherever your contributions are named.
settings_profile_avatar_desc: PNG, JPEG or WebP. Without a picture, your initials are shown.
settings_footer_notice_desc: An info icon at the end of the legal line links to the page about this software: its licence and source code. The licence requires it, so it is always shown and cannot be removed.
settings_navigation_intro: Entries shown in the desktop app bar and the mobile menu, in this order.
settings_home_intro: The page rendered at the site root (/).
settings_home_none: No home page set — visitors see a fallback index or the login page.
settings_branding_intro: Shown in the app bar and editor in place of the default mark. PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, or SVG — max 8 MB.
settings_branding_none: No custom logo set — the default mark is shown.
settings_branding_colors_intro: The accent and brand colours of the interface and of pages, in the light and the dark scheme.
settings_branding_accent_desc: Buttons, links, focus rings and what is selected. Each colour scheme gets the step of this colour that reads on its grounds.
settings_branding_accent_scheme_desc: Set by hand instead of generated from the accent. It has to read on the scheme’s grounds.
settings_branding_accent_shortfall: Too low contrast, so it can’t be saved: {pairs}.
settings_branding_brand_desc: Named colours authors can pick for pages, with a value for light and one for dark. Renaming a colour keeps it on the pages that use it.
settings_branding_brand_invalid: Every brand colour needs a name and a colour for each scheme.
settings_branding_brand_contrast: Neither text colour reads on it ({ratio}:1 at best), so a block filled with it needs its own text colour.
settings_branding_brand_contrast_light: In the light scheme neither text colour reads on it ({ratio}:1 at best), so a block filled with it needs its own text colour.
settings_branding_brand_contrast_dark: In the dark scheme neither text colour reads on it ({ratio}:1 at best), so a block filled with it needs its own text colour.
settings_branding_footer_desc: An optional background for the site footer. Its text takes whichever colour reads on it — that isn’t configurable.
settings_branding_footer_dark_desc: The same for readers in the dark scheme. Left unset, the footer stays plain there.
settings_branding_appbar_desc: An optional background for the bar at the top of the app. Its text, icons and controls take whichever colour reads on it, and the browser’s own chrome matches it.
settings_branding_appbar_dark_desc: The same for readers in the dark scheme. Left unset, the bar stays plain there.
settings_branding_preview_desc: The interface and a page in these colours, before they’re saved.
settings_branding_block_defaults_intro: What a block gets when it sets nothing of its own, per block-type group — steps and theme colours only, so it adapts to every colour scheme. The block settings show it as “Auto”; a block deviates only where it has a value of its own.
settings_branding_block_defaults_matrix_: Auto is the built-in default (in the tooltip). The page is the outermost flow: its block spacing applies wherever no container sets its own.
settings_branding_block_defaults_widths_: The reading column (Reading width), the wide band (Wide) and the outer cap a "Full" section fills. Empty is the built-in default; a page can override the reading and wide widths for itself.
settings_branding_block_defaults_gutters: The space between the page edge and the content per screen size — also the side padding of sections set to "Full". Auto is the built-in default; a page can override each screen size for itself.
settings_branding_block_defaults_error_i: The block defaults could not be read.
settings_branding_dark_logo_intro: Shown in place of the logo wherever the dark scheme is in use. PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, or SVG — max 8 MB.
settings_branding_dark_logo_none: No logo for dark — the logo is shown in both schemes.
settings_branding_ui_font_intro: The font used by the app's own interface — app bar, admin centre, buttons, menus, forms. Independent of the content typography below, so the interface can use a different font than page content if you want.
settings_branding_typography_intro: Define named styles (tokens) from system fonts or your hosted custom fonts, then assign them to the paragraph styles below. Styles with no token use the built-in defaults, so nothing changes until you assign one.
settings_branding_typography_tokens_empt: No tokens yet — add one below.
settings_branding_paragraph_styles_intro: The styles authors pick in the toolbar: each renders as one element (p, h1–h6) and takes its token’s look. Exactly one style per element is the default — the one Enter, a markdown # and a keyboard shortcut set.
settings_branding_paragraph_styles_defau: The default for this element — make another style the default to replace it.
settings_branding_paragraph_styles_delet: A default style can’t be deleted.
Blocks using this style fall back to their element’s default.
settings_branding_paragraph_styles_rende: The element the style renders as in the document. Fixed when the style is created.
Fixed at creation — content keeps its element.
settings_branding_paragraph_styles_token: The style’s look; without a token, its element’s built-in values.
settings_footer_intro: Global footer shown on every page. Link columns and the legal line reuse the same page-or-URL entry model as Navigation.
settings_footer_legal_intro: Impressum / privacy / contact — rendered as a strip at the bottom of the footer.
settings_footer_branding_intro: Any combination of logo, title, and tagline — each is optional. The logo is the site's global logo (set in Branding).
settings_fonts_intro: Self-hosted custom font families (woff2). Uploaded families become available wherever the Typography tool offers a font.
settings_fonts_variant_empty: No variants yet — add a woff2 file below.
settings_fonts_error_file_required: Choose a woff2 file to upload.
settings_styles_intro: Named styles editors can apply to content, and free CSS for everything else. Both take effect inside a page's content area only — the interface is never touched.
settings_page_layouts_intro: The layouts authors choose for a page. A page layout sets only the structure — columns per screen size, the space between them and how new sections start; the look follows the design. A page takes the values when it picks a layout: changes here reach existing pages only once the layout is applied there again.
settings_page_layouts_protected: Standard is always available: the layout every page can fall back to.
settings_page_layouts_delete_confirm: Pages that use it keep their values and show “Custom” from then on.
settings_page_layouts_description_hint: What the layout is for — for other admins and for AI agents.
settings_page_layouts_flow_note: Standard is the flow: blocks one after another in the reading column, without columns.
settings_page_layouts_span_hint: How wide a new section starts on a page with this layout.
settings_page_layouts_bleed_label: First section runs to the top edge
settings_styles_delete_confirm: This stylesheet and all of its named styles will be deleted. Content using one of them goes back to plain.
settings_styles_named_intro: Each style gets a fixed class when it is created. The label can change at any time, the class never can — content refers to the style, not to its name.
settings_styles_style_label_hint: How the style is offered when it is applied.
settings_styles_style_kind_hint: A text run wraps a stretch of text, a block wraps a whole block.
settings_styles_style_slug_hint: Made from the label, and fixed from then on.
settings_styles_style_slug_new_hint: Made from the label when you save, and fixed from then on.
settings_styles_style_css_hint: Declarations only, no braces — for example: background: var(--content-accent-soft);
settings_styles_style_delete_confirm: This style will be deleted. Content using it goes back to plain.
settings_styles_free_intro: For the cases and corrections named styles do not cover. Every rule is confined to the content area when you save, and none of it is offered for selection.
settings_styles_free_hint: Whole rules with selectors. @media, @container and @keyframes are allowed; imports and font faces are not.
settings_styles_css_top_level_nesting: A top-level selector cannot use "&". Nest the rule inside another one instead.
settings_styles_css_leading_combinator: A selector cannot start with a combinator.
settings_styles_css_empty_url: An empty url() is not allowed.
settings_styles_css_url_other_origin: url("{url}") points at another origin. Only same-origin paths starting with "/" are allowed.
settings_styles_css_url_not_same_origin: url("{url}") is not a same-origin path. Use an asset route starting with "/" (fonts belong in Settings → Fonts).
settings_styles_css_position_fixed: position: fixed is not allowed — it would place an element outside the content area. Use sticky or absolute.
settings_styles_css_z_index: z-index must be a plain number between {min} and {max}.
settings_styles_css_nested_keyframes: @keyframes cannot be nested inside a rule. Define it on its own.
settings_styles_css_keyframes_content: A @keyframes block may only contain keyframe selectors (from, to, a percentage).
settings_styles_css_keyframe_content: A keyframe may only contain declarations.
settings_styles_css_at_rule: @{name} is not allowed. Fonts belong in Settings → Fonts; imports and layers are not available.
settings_styles_css_declaration_outside_: A declaration must sit inside a rule.
settings_styles_css_animation_name: "{name}" is not a usable animation name.
settings_styles_css_unreadable_output: Compiled CSS could not be re-read: {reason}
settings_styles_css_escaped_scope: A rule escaped the content scope: {selector}
settings_styles_css_style_braces: A named style is a list of declarations — it cannot open or close a rule of its own. Remove the stray "{open}" or "{close}".
settings_styles_warn_literal_color: Fixed colour ({values}) — a --content token follows the reader's colour scheme, a fixed colour cannot.
settings_styles_warn_contrast_scheme_lig: On {background}, the text colour of light pages is hard to read (below 4.5:1).
settings_styles_warn_contrast_scheme_dar: On {background}, the text colour of dark pages is hard to read (below 4.5:1).
settings_styles_warn_contrast_scheme_bot: On {background}, the text colour of both light and dark pages is hard to read (below 4.5:1). Set a text colour of your own as well.
settings_styles_preview_intro: This stylesheet's named styles on a sample page.
settings_styles_preview_lead: A paragraph of body text, so it is clear how a style behaves among ordinary words.
settings_styles_preview_empty: No named styles to show yet.
settings_navigation_tree_empty: No entries yet — add one below.
settings_navigation_tree_group_empty: No links in this group yet.

settings_users_error_exists: A user with that email already exists.
settings_users_error_own_admin_role: You can't remove your own admin role.
settings_users_error_own_deactivate: You can't deactivate your own account.

settings_users_error_password_too_common: That password is too easy to guess — choose another.
settings_namespaces_intro: A namespace groups content under a URL prefix (project-a/slug) and sets the default access level new content in it starts with. The default namespace has no prefix and is where new content lands unless reassigned.
settings_namespaces_delete_confirm_body: Delete this namespace? Its content moves to the default namespace — old URLs under this prefix will 404.
settings_namespaces_widen_public: {count} pages and documents take this namespace's access level and become public with it — visible to signed-out visitors too.
settings_namespaces_widen_internal: {count} pages and documents take this namespace's access level and become visible to every signed-in user.
settings_namespaces_members_hint: Members can read this namespace's content by default (unless a page/document narrows its own access further). Owners and admins always have access, regardless of membership.

content_scheme_finding_border: {block}: border reads at {ratio}:1 on a {ground} page (needs 3:1)

content_scheme_apply_failed: Could not change the colour scheme.

settings_color_scheme_default_desc: Pages with a colour scheme of their own keep it.
settings_color_scheme_report_desc: Colours on pages that follow the default and may not read once they adapt. Only pages you can see are listed.
settings_color_scheme_report_summary: {inheriting} pages follow the default, {pinned} choose their own.

settings_color_scheme_check_report: I reviewed the pages with findings, and kept the ones that should stay light

editor_access_control_restricted_hint: You (the owner) and admins always have access. Select who else can read:
editor_access_control_restricted_owner_o: Only you (the owner) and admins have access.
editor_access_control_no_other_users: No other users to share with.
editor_access_control_namespace_hint: Moving this page changes its URL — the old link will stop working.
editor_access_control_error_generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
editor_access_control_namespace_members_: This namespace has no members yet.
editor_access_control_share_links_empty: No share links yet. Anyone with a share link can view this page without signing in.
editor_access_control_share_link_created: Copy this link now — it won't be shown again.
editor_access_control_share_link_revoke_: Revoke this share link? Anyone using it will lose access immediately.
editor_access_control_error_share_link_c: Could not copy the link. Select it in the field and copy it yourself.
editor_lock_blocked_body: {name} currently has this page open for editing.
editor_lock_blocked_stale: Their session looks inactive, so you should be able to take over shortly.

settings_schema_properties_intro: Define the semantic properties used across the wiki. Defining a property gives it a human-readable label and a datatype, and makes it appear as a suggestion when authors annotate pages. Properties can still be used ad hoc without being defined here.
settings_schema_groups_intro: Property groups are named, globally reusable groups of property definitions, each with a key. A property's full identity is key:property (e.g. core:deadline) — every property belongs to exactly one group.
settings_schema_classes_intro: Classes form a single-parent hierarchy: node → the node types (page, document) → your own classes such as "work package". Every node carries exactly one class, at least its node type. A class hangs under a node type or another class, which decides which nodes it can be assigned to, and may carry a property group whose properties show as first-class fields. Editors assign classes in the editor's properties dialog.
settings_schema_classes_inherited_hint: Nodes of this class also get the fields of: {groups}
settings_schema_classes_parent_hint: A node type (page, document) or an existing class. The parent decides which nodes this class can be assigned to.
settings_schema_classes_core_locked: This is a core class: its key and parent are fixed and it cannot be deleted. Label, description, property group and overview page can be changed.
settings_schema_classes_delete_in_use_ti: Remove this class from all nodes before deleting it.
settings_schema_classes_group_hint: The group's properties render as first-class fields on every node of this class.
settings_schema_classes_overview_hint: Optional shortcut to a page listing this class — overview pages otherwise emerge from a query block filtering by class.
settings_schema_classes_description_plac: What kind of thing this class represents
settings_schema_relationships_intro: Relationship types are named, globally-reusable edge kinds for typed links between pages (e.g. "is author of"). Use "Manage properties" on a type to choose which individual properties an edge of that type carries.
settings_schema_relationships_properties: Choose which properties an edge of this type carries. Properties are individually selected — a relationship type is not tied to a whole property group.

capability_height_info: The block is at least this tall, even when its content is shorter — a hero, say. The screen height follows the reader's device.
capability_spacing_block_space_hint: Default space above every block in this area.
capability_spacing_gutter_info: The space between the page edge and the content at this screen size — also the side padding of sections set to "Full". Auto is the site's page margin for this screen size; each screen size stands on its own.

editor_placement_move_info: Where the block belongs on the page: the column beside it, the section before or after, or a section of its own. It always lands at the end of the column.
editor_placement_align_info: How the block sits in its column: at the start, in the middle or at the end — then as wide as its content — or across its full width. Auto fills the column.
editor_placement_align_info_card: How the card sits in its column: at the start, in the middle, at the end or across its full width. Auto follows the cell’s alignment.
editor_placement_align_info_image: How the image sits in its column when it is narrower. Auto is the middle; the image sets its own width.
editor_flex_item_size_info: Along the container’s direction. Auto: as large as its content. Fill: shares the free space with the other filling cells, by weight. Fixed: a size of its own, which wraps or yields rather than overflowing.
editor_flex_item_size_auto_title: Auto · as large as its content
editor_flex_item_weight_info: How much of the free space the cell takes against the other filling cells: 2 is twice as much as 1.
editor_flex_item_basis_info: Never wider than the row: where it doesn’t fit, the cell wraps where the container wraps, and yields where it doesn’t.
editor_flex_item_self_info: Where the cell sits across the container’s direction. Auto follows the container’s alignment.

editor_page_layout_info: The site’s page layouts (Settings → Page layouts). A layout’s values are copied into the page when you choose it; later changes to it reach the page only once you apply it here again. Custom: columns of your own.
editor_page_layout_to_columns_desc: All of the page's blocks go into one section, in its first column. You can undo this.
editor_page_layout_to_flow_desc: The content of every section ends up one after another, in order. The sections' surface, spacing and span go. You can undo this.
editor_page_columns_info: How many columns this screen size has, and their proportions. A smaller screen size never has more columns than a larger one. Fewer columns on the desktop merge the content of the columns that go, without losing it.
editor_page_columns_ratios_info: How the width is shared between the columns, as a ratio: 3 and 2 give the first column three fifths.

editor_grid_columns_auto_tablet: Auto · as on the desktop, {count} columns
editor_grid_columns_info: How many columns the grid has at this screen size, and their proportions. With fewer columns than on the desktop, the cells flow into them in reading order, and merged cells and row heights don't apply.
editor_page_width_custom_title: A width of this page's own
editor_page_width_read_info: How wide text and every block without a section width of its own can get. Auto is the site's block default. Applies to all screen sizes.
editor_page_width_wide_info: How wide sections set to "Wide" can get — never narrower than the reading width. Auto is the site's block default. Applies to all screen sizes.
editor_page_background_info: The whole page's background: a theme colour that text and links stay readable on, following every colour scheme. Applies to all screen sizes.
